thread:
jamie: FYI handoff — ongoing rate surge affecting embeddings pipeline. Alerts firing for embeddings-queue-length and embedding-worker-503s. Customer impact: elevated p99 embedding latency (2.2s -> ~6s) and a small % of requests returning 503. Taking primary for next 4h then passing to @sara.

jamie: Current state:
- alerts: embeddings-queue-length (>2000) on eu-west and us-east, embedding-worker-503s on us-east
- degraded region: us-east most impacted, eu-west seeing increased queue but processing slowly
- root cause hypothesis: sudden burst from a downstream partner causing very large batch sizes + KV store throttling (redis UOPS high)
- customer-visible: background index jobs delayed, some user-facing recommendations slowed, no data loss reported

ops-bot: [ALERT] embeddings-queue-length (eu-west) triggered at 2026-03-13T23:48:12Z — threshold 1500 (current 2187)
ops-bot: [ALERT] embedding-worker-503s (us-east) triggered at 2026-03-13T23:49:02Z — 503 rate 4.1%

oncall-bot: Runbook link: https://wiki.internal/redwood/runbooks/embeddings-queue (use section "Mitigation -> Immediate")

jamie: Mitigations already in progress:
- scaled embedding-worker pool in us-east from 12 -> 28 instances (rolled by autoscaler override) using: `infractl scale cluster embeddings-us-east --replicas 28`
- enabled burst capacity for dedicated customers to allow short spikes: `redwoodctl capacity allow-burst --pool embeddings --duration 10m`
- applied soft-rate-limit on partner API key: `ratelimitctl set partner-123 100rps` (partner agreed to temporary throttle)
- enabled fallback route to quantized-embed-small model for best-effort requests: `routingctl set-policy embeddings route:quant-small when queue>1000`

jamie: Open actions / monitoring:
- watching redis UOPS and eviction rate (olga)
- observe p99 and 95 across routes (mike)
- coord with partner to reduce batch sizes (contacted partner + emailed partner-engineering)

sara: taking over primary at 00:30 UTC. Thanks jamie — I have the runbook open. Quick Q: which customer tenants are seeing 503s?

jamie: olga has list — primary affected tenants: seatly-app, docsynth (transactions mainly background), partner-analytics (best-effort requests)

olga: Confirmed — top 10 failing tenants: seatly-app (2.4% errors), docsynth (1.7%), partner-analytics (3.8%). I pushed a temporary client-side retry hint to seatly-app last 15m to reduce immediate error surface.

mike: I set up temporary dashboard widget: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/d/embeddings/surge-quickview — includes queue length, worker pods, redis ops, and p99 latency. Watching tail errors and request traces.

sara: On the runbook — steps I plan to run next:
1) Verify autoscaler health and node pressure (if node CPU >85% consider adding nodes)
2) If redis eviction spikes continue, switch to read-replica for hot keys: `kvctl promote-replica redis-eu-read`
3) Keep fallback routing enabled, but start a gradual rollback if queue falls under 800 for 10m

jamie: Note: we haven't enabled full global rate-limiting yet because it affects paid SLAs. Try to keep throttles targeted to partner keys only.

olga: Also — trace id pattern shows large batch sizes from partner-analytics: header `X-Batch-Size: 512` in many requests. Partner acknowledged and says they can ship a patch to limit to 64 within 20m.

mike: Observed side-effect: autothrottle for continuous-batching is dropping throughput on small requests when queue >1500. That explains some latency inflation; routing to quantized-embed-small helps but reduces quality. Communicating tradeoff to docsynth PM.

sara: I'll be primary for the next 4 hours. mike you're secondary and on pager for 30m in case I step out. jamie — when you unplug, confirm your notes are in the runbook page.

jamie: Confirmed — updated runbook with exact commands and who I paged. Added `mitigation_log` section with timestamps.

olga: Customer comms: copies of the initial incident message were sent to seatly-app support and docsynth eng lead. Partner-analytics was told to throttle; they acknowledged.

mike: If we see queue growth after partner patch window (20m), escalate to infra SRE to add nodes and consider temporary read-only cache for hot prefixes. Command: `infractl add-node --pool embeddings-us-east --type g5-2x` (pre-approval pending)

sara: Coverage gap note: between 03:00-04:00 UTC there is only 1 SRE on-call in our rotation due to holidays — I've asked ops to keep an extra standby. If that can't be filled, I'll keep an ear on pager and adjust escalation to on-call-lead.

ops-bot: [INFO] scheduled maintenance in us-east for 04:00 UTC — no expected impact but FYI for capacity planning

jamie: Leaving detailed checklist for you, sara: check `redis evictions`, `worker pod restarts`, `traffic split metrics`, and `partner backoff status`. If errors >5% for 15m, escalate to SEV-2 and call bridge.

sara: Got it. I'll post updates every 10m or on key transitions. Thanks all, taking over now. :thumbsup:

mike: Standing by — will post traces if anything spikes.

olga: I'll keep customer contacts updated if error rate stays >1% for another 10m.

sara: Handoff complete. Logs/commands saved in runbook at https://wiki.internal/redwood/runbooks/embeddings-queue#handoff-notes

jamie: Thanks team — leaving bridge for backup, reachable on-call via pager.

ops-bot: [RESOLVE-INFO] embeddings-queue-length (eu-west) cleared at 2026-03-13T23:58:40Z (queue 720) — monitor closely for re-trigger

sara: noted, continuing to monitor."
